primary.title: The Divine Comedy
primary.author: Dante Alighieri
primary.rationale: Dante's epic poem is his most famous work and a foundational text of Italian literature. It is widely available in numerous editions and translations.

primary.title: La Vita Nuova
primary.author: Dante Alighieri
primary.rationale: This early work by Dante combines poetry and prose, detailing his love for Beatrice. It is a significant text for understanding his early life and poetic development.

primary.title: De Monarchia
primary.author: Dante Alighieri
primary.rationale: A political treatise in Latin, De Monarchia outlines Dante's views on the relationship between secular and ecclesiastical power. It is crucial for understanding his political philosophy.

secondary.title: The Cambridge Companion to Dante
secondary.author: Ronald B. Herzman
secondary.rationale: This is a comprehensive collection of essays by leading scholars covering various aspects of Dante's life, works, and influence, published by a major academic press.

secondary.title: Dante: The Poet of the Divine Comedy
secondary.author: Erich Auerbach
secondary.rationale: While published before 1976, Auerbach's work is a seminal and enduring critical analysis of Dante's masterpiece, often cited in later scholarship. It provides deep insights into the poem's literary and theological dimensions.

secondary.title: Dante's Epic Journeys: From the Inferno to the Purgatorio
secondary.author: Giuseppe Mazzotta
secondary.rationale: Mazzotta is a prominent Dante scholar, and this book offers a detailed scholarly examination of key themes and structures within the Divine Comedy.

suggestions.notes: The primary sources are foundational texts by Dante. Secondary sources include a major companion volume and influential critical works by leading scholars, with one seminal work predating the 1976 cutoff due to its lasting importance.
